detail: MIT Libraries identifies the 1912 Gurlitt mosque plate from Die Baukunst Konstantinopels and explicitly states public domain with no use restrictions.
Public-domain Gurlitt exterior complex plan identifies the cloistered mosque and madrasa arrangement.
Fatih mosque album pp. 214–216 describes pale cut stone, five portico domes, four half-domes, lower arcades and nine-sided courtyard fountain.
The Fatih architectural documentation identifies the cut limestone and 12 m diameter dome on a hexagonal support, five-arched entrance and 25-bay enclosure.
The architectural study records the cross-sectional arrangement, one minaret balcony, side buttresses and off-center ablution fountain.
